name: YeboMart
audience: Shop owners and retail teams managing the till, stock and daily close.

features.title: Mobile point of sale for shops | YeboMart
features.description: Ring up shop sales with a mobile till and keep the transaction linked to stock and business records.
features.headline: Keep the sale connected to the rest of your shop.
features.intro:
At the counter, the next action should be obvious: select the items, check the total and record the sale. YeboMart gives shop staff a mobile point-of-sale workflow built around that routine.

The till sits alongside the shop’s stock and operating records. Use one sale record for the transaction instead of rewriting the same sale into a separate stock book and end-of-day tally.
paragraphs: At the counter, the next action should be obvious: select the items, check the total and record the sale. YeboMart gives shop staff a mobile point-of-sale workflow built around that routine.
The till sits alongside the shop’s stock and operating records. Use one sale record for the transaction instead of rewriting the same sale into a separate stock book and end-of-day tally.
features.audience: Shop owners and retail teams managing the till, stock and daily close.

benefits.title: A practical till
benefits.body: Find the product by scanning or selecting it, then review the basket. Check the quantity and price before completing the transaction.

benefits.title: A sale with a staff record
benefits.body: Use the configured cashier access so the business can identify the person responsible for the transaction and later adjustments.

benefits.title: The receipt and next step
benefits.body: Complete the sale through the available payment and receipt workflow. Keep the record available when the customer or owner has a question.

steps: Open the till with the appropriate access.
Select items and check the basket.
Record the sale and issue its receipt.
features.limitations: Available payment methods, receipt options and offline behaviour depend on the configured device and services. Do not treat an unsynchronised record as confirmed server processing.
features.example: A cashier selling several everyday items can check the basket once, record the transaction and let the connected stock and sales records reflect that sale.
features.availability: implemented; production availability must be checked by release owner

features.title: Inventory and stock receiving | YeboMart
features.description: Keep stock quantities, receiving and movements alongside shop sales in YeboMart.
features.headline: Know what changed in the stock count.
features.intro:
An empty shelf is easier to investigate when the stock count has a history. YeboMart connects inventory with the transactions and receiving work that change it.

Use the stock record to review what is on hand, what arrived and what moved. Keep product setup and physical counts accurate so the information is useful when deciding what needs attention or another order.
paragraphs: An empty shelf is easier to investigate when the stock count has a history. YeboMart connects inventory with the transactions and receiving work that change it.

Use the stock record to review what is on hand, what arrived and what moved. Keep product setup and physical counts accurate so the information is useful when deciding what needs attention or another order.
features.audience: Shop owners and retail teams managing the till, stock and daily close.

benefits.title: Follow movements
benefits.body: Review the changes behind a quantity rather than treating the latest number as the whole story. Sales and stock work should remain connected.

benefits.title: Record incoming goods
benefits.body: Receive stock through the intended workflow when a delivery arrives. Check the products and quantities against what was actually supplied.

benefits.title: Plan the next order
benefits.body: Use the available low-stock and reorder information to decide what to investigate. Check supplier and stock details before taking further action.

features.limitations: Inventory depends on complete receiving and adjustment records. Reorder information supports a purchasing decision; it is not proof that a supplier order was placed.
features.example: When a delivery arrives, record the quantity actually received rather than the quantity expected. Review the resulting count before returning the product to regular sale.
features.availability: implemented; production availability must be checked by release owner

features.title: Cash-up and cashier accountability | YeboMart
features.description: Review opening float, recorded takings and counted cash when closing a YeboMart cash session.
features.headline: Close the till with a count you can compare.
features.intro:
A busy day does not explain the difference between the drawer and the expected cash. YeboMart provides a cash-up workflow that connects the opening float, recorded activity and closing count.

Use staff access and the audit record to follow who made a sale or adjustment. A variance is a starting point for checking the day’s records, not a conclusion about why the figures differ.
paragraphs: A busy day does not explain the difference between the drawer and the expected cash. YeboMart provides a cash-up workflow that connects the opening float, recorded activity and closing count.
Use staff access and the audit record to follow who made a sale or adjustment. A variance is a starting point for checking the day’s records, not a conclusion about why the figures differ.
features.audience: Shop owners and retail teams managing the till, stock and daily close.

benefits.title: Open with the actual float
benefits.body: Record the money put into the till at the start. A reliable opening amount gives the closing comparison a defined starting point.

benefits.title: Keep staff activity attributable
benefits.body: Use the cashier’s configured access for sales, voids and refunds. Review the records when an amount needs explaining.

benefits.title: Compare before closing
benefits.body: Count the cash and inspect the difference from the expected amount. Follow the available report and audit detail before deciding what needs correction.

steps: Record sales under the right staff access.
Review variance and the day’s record.
features.limitations: Cash-up reports depend on accurate entries. A variance does not itself establish theft, loss or a particular person’s responsibility.
features.example: At close, the manager counts the drawer and compares it with the recorded cash position. Any difference can then be checked against the relevant transactions and adjustments.
